book.title: CVC - Short Vowels
book.source: Science of Reading Level 2 Teacher Guide

units.title: Consonants and vowels
units.summary: Mini-lesson 1. Review what a syllable is (a word part with one vowel sound; count by clapping), then vowels (a, e, i, o, u) against consonants. Every syllable must have a vowel sound. For now students focus on the short vowel sounds: apple, edge, igloo, otter, umbrella.

lessons.title: Count syllables
lessons.notes: Say a word, repeat it, clap the syllables, and ask how many vowel sounds it has: window, step, crocodile, basket.

lessons.title: Review vowels and consonants
lessons.notes: Letter tiles labelled C and V; vowel sounds are not blocked by the lips, tongue or teeth.

lessons.title: Short vowel sounds
lessons.notes: /ă/ apple, /ĕ/ edge, /ĭ/ igloo, /ŏ/ otter, /ŭ/ umbrella.

objectives.text: clap the syllables in words like window, step and basket
name the vowels a, e, i, o, u and tell them from consonants
say that every syllable needs one vowel sound

units.title: Closed syllables
units.summary: Mini-lesson 2. A closed syllable ends with a consonant, which closes in the vowel so it says its short sound (sip, camp). A syllable that ends in a vowel, like he, is not closed; that comes later. Students build words with letter tiles and say whether each is closed and how they know.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Say a word, repeat it, then say its vowel sound: sad, rip.

lessons.title: Closed syllable poster
lessons.notes: Consonants are blue magnets, vowels yellow; the consonant closes in the vowel.

lessons.title: Build and decide
lessons.notes: Build sip, camp and he; is it closed and what will the vowel say.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Build further words, label C and V, and say closed or not closed; this is identifying, not reading.

lessons.title: Finger-spell and map
lessons.notes: Segment map as /m/ /ă/ /p/, push three boxes or magnets, match a letter to each sound.

objectives.text: tell a closed syllable from a syllable that ends in a vowel
explain that the consonant closes in the vowel so it says a short sound
break a word like map into three sounds and match each to a letter

units.title: Short a
units.summary: CVC words with short a, plus the "whiny a" before n and m (jam, can, van, ham). Word endings: -at, -an, -ap, -ag, -ad, -am, -ab (also -ax). High-frequency words: at, am, an, can, man, had; as, has. Mouth wide open for /ă/.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Listen for the /ă/ sound in spoken words and give a thumbs up; mouth position and a key-word chant.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: Letter tile and key-word chant: apple, apple, /ă/, /ă/, /ă/.

lessons.title: Encoding (spelling)
lessons.notes: Stretch the word, tap the sounds, match each sound to a letter; is it a closed syllable and what does the vowel say.

lessons.title: Decoding (reading)
lessons.notes: Touch and say, blending sound by sound; successive blending and backward decoding for readers who struggle.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Decode and encode from the word list, then dictation of one or two sentences.

lessons.title: Common word endings
lessons.notes: -at, -an, -ap, -ag, -ad, -am, -ab.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: Regular: at, am, an, can, man, had. New learning: as, has (s spells /z/ at the end of a word)

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Word sorts, onset-rime match, word chains, reading sentences; independent practice in the student workbook.

objectives.text: hear the short a sound in words like cat, fan, bag and map
spell words like sad, rat, jam and tag by tapping out the sounds
read words in the -at, -an and -ap families by blending
read the common words at, am, an, can, had and has

units.title: All short vowels together
units.summary: Lesson 3.6. No new teaching: students read and spell CVC words and sentences with all five short vowels mixed. Each day: review the concepts, one phonemic awareness drill (isolate the vowel, segment, add, delete or change a sound), guided decoding and encoding, then independent practice. Irregular high-frequency words are taught by marking the unexpected letter with a heart.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness drills
lessons.notes: Isolate the vowel sound, segment words with manipulatives, or add, delete and change a sound (cap to map).

lessons.title: Mixed decoding and encoding
lessons.notes: Guided practice with all vowels together; independent workbook pages and decodable sentences.

lessons.title: Irregular high-frequency words
lessons.notes: Say, use in a sentence, break into sounds, mark the unexpected letter with a heart.

lessons.title: More activities

objectives.text: read and spell words that mix all five short vowels

replaces: Closed Syllables · CVC Words: All Short Vowels Together

units.title: Suffix -s
units.summary: Lessons 4A and 4B. A suffix is added to the end of a base word. -s on a noun makes it more than one (cat, cats); -s on an action word shows it is happening now (run, runs). The suffix -s says /s/ or /z/ (cats, dogs).

lessons.title: Suffix -s on nouns
lessons.notes: Build cat and cats with a purple -s magnet; base word and suffix; listen for /s/ or /z/: bugs, pets, pens, cups, mugs, cubs, maps.

lessons.title: Suffix -s on verbs
lessons.notes: Run and runs, jog and jogs; use in sentences and listen for the suffix in fits, hums, fills, subs, pats.

objectives.text: name the base word and the suffix in words like cats and runs
add -s to make a word mean more than one, as in cat and cats
hear that -s can sound like /s/ or /z/ in bugs and pets
use -s on an action word so the sentence sounds right, such as she runs

book.title: Consonant Digraphs
book.source: Science of Reading Level 3 Teacher Guide

units.title: sh
units.summary: Lesson 5.1. A digraph is two consonants that together make one sound; sh, th and ch are sometimes called the "h brothers". Word lists use short vowels only. Word endings -ash, -ish, -ush. High-frequency words: she, push (the e in she and the u in push are irregular for now, so mark a heart). Pacing: about a week per digraph in kindergarten, 2 to 3 days in first grade.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear /sh/ at the start and end of words.

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build words with a sh tile; sound boxes show two letters for one sound.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Decode and encode from the word list; dictation and sentence reading.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: she, push; heart over the irregular letter.

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Sort words by ending -ash, -ish, -ush; dictation, e.g. "A fish is on a dish".

objectives.text: say that the letters sh together make one sound
read words like ship, shop, fish, dish and rush
spell words with sh, such as shed, shin, gash and wish
read the common words she and push

units.title: th
units.summary: Lesson 5.2. th is made by resting the teeth on the tongue and has two sounds: voiced (this, that, breathe, felt in the throat) and unvoiced (with, thumb, path). Most high-frequency function words that start with th are voiced. Word list uses short vowels only. High-frequency words: the, that, this, then, with, than, them, both.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness and background
lessons.notes: Voiced and unvoiced th; hand on the throat.

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build words with the th tile and ask which sound it makes.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Decode and encode from the word list; dictation and sentence reading.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: the (heart over the e if it sounds like /ŭ/), that, this, then, with.

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Sort voiced and unvoiced th; sort by where th sits in the word.

objectives.text: tell the voiced th in this and that from the unvoiced th in thin and path
read words like thin, bath, with, then and them
spell words with th, such as thud, math and moth
read the common words the, that, this and with

units.title: ch
units.summary: Lesson 5.3. ch is a stopping sound; use a chopping arm motion. It is the unvoiced partner of /j/, so the two are often confused. Word list uses short vowels only. Dictation and sentence reading are included.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Build thin, that and ship and say which th sound is used.

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build words with the ch tile; ch as a stopping sound with a chopping motion.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Decode and encode from the word list; dictation and sentence reading.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: Taught with the encoding steps and practised on note cards.

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Dictation; read sentences, circle the subject and underline the predicate.

objectives.text: hear the stopping /ch/ sound at the start and end of words
read words like chip, chop, chat, much and rich
spell words with ch, such as chin, chill, such and inch
tell /ch/ in chin from /j/ in jam

units.title: wh
units.summary: Mini-lesson 5.4. For most speakers wh sounds the same as w; long ago it sounded like /hw/. Only a few words can be read at this point (when, what, whip, which, whisk, whiff), so introduce it briefly and point out new wh words as they come. Most question words (who, what, when, where, why) use wh. High-frequency words: what, which (what is irregular: the a spells /ŭ/).

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: Some sounds use more than one letter; wh can also represent /w/.

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build whip, whisk and whiff with the wh tile; compare w and wh if you hear a difference.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: what and which; mark a heart over the irregular letter.

lessons.title: Dictation and sentence reading
lessons.notes: "What is that?" "Which box is his?"

objectives.text: read wh words like when, whip, whisk and whiff
know that wh and w can spell the same /w/ sound
read the question words what, when and which

units.title: Review all digraphs
units.summary: Lesson 5.5. Read and spell sh, th, ch and wh words together, with practice to automaticity. Irregular high-frequency words: what, the. Dictation sentences include: A bad gash is on my shin. A fish is on a dish. I wish I had a ship. I shut the shed. That is a thin kid. I can dip a chip. I am on a path.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Mixed decoding and encoding
lessons.notes: Words with sh, th, ch and wh, sorted by digraph.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: what, the; heart over the irregular letter.

lessons.title: Dictation
lessons.notes: Say the sentence, count the words, write it, correct.

objectives.text: read words that mix sh, th, ch and wh without stopping to work them out
write dictated sentences such as "I wish I had a ship"
sort words by the digraph they contain

replaces: Closed Syllables · Consonant Digraphs: Review all

units.title: Suffix -es
units.summary: Lesson 6. When a base word ends in /s/, /z/, /sh/ or /ch/ (dish, box, buzz, lunch), the suffix -es is used instead of -s, because /s/ and /z/ cannot follow those sounds; the extra vowel sound is needed to say the word (dishes). Spelling of doubled letters is taught later (lesson 9).

lessons.title: Introduce
lessons.notes: Build dish, try -s ("dishz"), then use the purple -es suffix to make dishes.

lessons.title: Listen for the extra vowel sound
lessons.notes: Say words with the base and suffix separated.

lessons.title: Sort
lessons.notes: Words that take -s and words that take -es.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell plural nouns and verbs with -es.

objectives.text: add -es to words that end in sh, ch, x and s, like dishes and boxes
explain why dishz cannot be said and dishes can
spell words like wishes, catches and fixes

book.title: Blends
book.source: Science of Reading Level 4 Teacher Guide

units.title: Beginning blends
units.summary: Lesson 7.1. A consonant blend is two consonants side by side that each keep their own sound (unlike digraphs). Beginning blends: R blends (fr, gr, br, pr, cr, tr, dr), L blends (fl, gl, bl, pl, cl) and S blends (sp, st, sl, sn, sm, sc, sk). Reading a word with four sounds is hard at first, so use sound boxes and finger spelling. Irregular words: want, from. Sentences: Fred has a frog. Stan is glad. Plug this in.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Build chip: closed syllable, short vowel, which letters make one sound.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Segment four-sound words with bingo chips.

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build blend words (frog, glad, drum, flip) and read each sound in the blend.

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Decode and encode from the word list; dictation and sentence reading.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: want, from.

lessons.title: Dictation
lessons.notes: e.g. "I can hit the drum." "A van did crash."

objectives.text: name the two sounds heard in a blend such as fr, gl or st
read words like frog, glad, drum, stop and flip
spell words that start with blends, such as clap, plan, snap and trip

replaces: Closed Syllables · Digraph & Triple Blends (str, spr, spl, scr)

units.title: Ending blends
units.summary: Lesson 7.2. Ending blends: mp, nt, nd, lt, ld, lf, lp, ft, ct, st, sp, pt (nk comes later). Blends can come before or after the vowel in a syllable. Review at the end of the level: read and spell words with short vowels, digraphs and blends together to automaticity.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Build flash: which letters are a blend (fl) and which make one sound (sh).

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build words with ending blends (lamp, hand, felt, gift, mask).

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Decode and encode from the word list; dictation and sentence reading.

lessons.title: Mixed review
lessons.notes: Read and spell words with short vowels, digraphs and blends together.

objectives.text: read words that end in blends like lamp, hand, belt, gift and mask
spell words such as jump, tent, best and soft by listening for each sound at the end
read words that mix digraphs and blends, like chimp and shrub
read sentences with short vowels, digraphs and blends smoothly

book.title: Closed Syllable Rules
book.source: Science of Reading Level 5 Teacher Guide

units.title: Suffix -ed
units.summary: Lesson 8. Suffix -ed is added to action words to make the past tense and says /t/, /d/ or /id/ (jumped, planted). Review the terms base and suffix first. Teach -ed on closed syllables with a simple base (jump, planted); the doubling rule and the -ing suffix are practised with it.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Base word and suffix, with -s for plurals and verbs.

lessons.title: Introduce -ed
lessons.notes: Build jump and jumped; yesterday I jumped in the pond.

lessons.title: Three sounds of -ed
lessons.notes: Sort words by /t/, /d/ and /id/ (planted).

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell words with -ed; sentences.

objectives.text: say that -ed shows something already happened
hear -ed say /t/, /d/ or /id/ in jumped, rubbed and planted
add -ed to action words like jump, plant and help
name the base word in words like jumped and landed

replaces: Closed Syllables · Morphology Rule: Doubling Rule

units.title: ll, ff, ss, zz (the floss rule)
units.summary: Lesson 9. When a one-syllable word ends in f, l, s or z right after a short vowel, double the letter (floss, hill, kiss, buzz). No doubling after a long vowel or a consonant. Exceptions: bus, gas, if. A checklist poster has students ask each question. High-frequency words: will, well, still (also all, fall, small, call).

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Listen for short vowels in mask, tell, meal, dress, chase, chill, felt, mile, shock, stuff.

lessons.title: Introduce the rule
lessons.notes: Three things must happen before the last letter is doubled; sort words with double letters.

lessons.title: Model and guided practice
lessons.notes: Run the checklist for each word, then add the double letter or not.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: will, well, still.

lessons.title: Dictation
lessons.notes: Sentences from the word list.

objectives.text: double f, l, s or z at the end of a short-vowel word, as in hill and miss
decide whether a word needs double letters, using the checklist
read words like stuff, spill, fuzz and dress
name the exceptions bus, gas and if

replaces: Closed Syllables · Double Consonants: ll, ff, ss, zz

units.title: ck
units.summary: Lesson 10. When a one-syllable word ends in /k/ right after a short vowel, spell it ck (duck, pack, stuck); after a long vowel or a consonant, use k (milk, disk, dusk). Very like the floss rule. Beginning /k/: use k when e, i or y follows, otherwise c.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Use the floss poster questions to decide whether a final letter is doubled.

lessons.title: Introduce the rule
lessons.notes: ck after a short vowel, k after a consonant or long vowel.

lessons.title: Model and guided practice
lessons.notes: Sort and spell words like disk, pack, stuck, milk, dusk, duck.

lessons.title: Dictation
lessons.notes: Sentences from the word list.

objectives.text: choose ck or k at the end of a word by checking what comes right before it
read words like pack, kick, duck, milk and desk
spell words like sock, neck, risk and tusk
use k before e, i or y at the start of a word, as in kid and keg

units.title: tch
units.summary: Lesson 11. When a one-syllable word ends in /ch/ right after a short vowel, spell it tch (patch, clutch); otherwise ch (pinch, punch). tch is a digraph used only at the end of a one-syllable word. Review letters A to Z, sh, th, ch and ck.

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Build words and decide ck or k.

lessons.title: Introduce the rule
lessons.notes: Check the sound right before /ch/: short vowel means tch.

lessons.title: Model and guided practice
lessons.notes: Sort and spell pinch, clutch, patch and punch.

lessons.title: Dictation
lessons.notes: Sentences from the word list.

objectives.text: choose tch or ch at the end of a word by checking the sound before it
read words like match, stitch, lunch and bench
spell words like catch, fetch, pinch and hutch
explain why patch has tch and punch does not

units.title: ild, old, ost, olt, ind
units.summary: Lesson 12. These closed syllables are exceptions: the vowel is long even though a consonant closes it in (wild, cold, most, bolt, kind). High-frequency words: find, kind, old, told, most (also cold, hold, mind). Sentences: Did you find it? That child is kind. The cold is wild!

lessons.title: Warm up and review
lessons.notes: Visual drill (flip letters, students say the sound) and auditory drill (say a sound, students write the letter).

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Segment words with bingo chips and ask questions about each sound.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: Closed syllables usually say a short vowel; these word endings are the exceptions.

lessons.title: Model and guided practice
lessons.notes: Build words ending ild, old, olt, ind and ost.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: find, kind, old, told, most.

lessons.title: Dictation
lessons.notes: Sentences from the word list.

objectives.text: read the long vowel in wild, cold, bolt, kind and most
recognise the endings ild, old, olt, ind and ost
spell words like child, gold, bolt and mind
read the common words find, kind, old, told and most

replaces: Closed Syllables · Exceptions: ild, old, ost, ind, olt

units.title: ng and nk
units.summary: Lesson 13 ("Ring in the sink"). The ng and nk endings: /ĭ/, ang and ank say /ă/. May be split into two lessons, one for ng and one for nk. Phonemic awareness: take away the first sounds to leave ink or ang (sink, stink; tank, bunk, think, bang, sang, hung, thing, wrong). Closed-closed words are divided between the two consonants (VCCV) and, for three consonants, usually after the first (VCCCV), keeping digraphs and blends together as in pump-kin.

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Read the word endings -ind, -ild, -old, -olt and -ost.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Say a word, take away the sounds before the ending (stink to ink).

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: ng and nk with short vowels; ring in the sink.

lessons.title: Model and guided practice
lessons.notes: Build and read ng and nk words; sentences.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: bring, thing, think, thank, drink, sing, long.

objectives.text: read words ending in ng and nk, like ring, sang, sink and tank
hear the vowel sound before ng and nk in words like sing and bank
spell words like song, king, drink and trunk

replaces: Closed Syllables · -ng and -nk (& new grapheme: ng)

book.title: VCe - Long Vowels with 'e'
book.source: Science of Reading Level 6 Teacher Guide

units.title: Introduction to Silent e
units.summary: Mini-lesson 1. Review: a closed syllable gives a short vowel (shop); a syllable that ends in a vowel can say its name (she). Silent e is the first job introduced: it tells the reader that another vowel will say its long sound. The silent e has many jobs: it makes vowels long, makes c say /s/ and g say /j/, keeps words from ending in v, keeps a word from looking plural, and gives the voiced th. Students review short vowels (apple, Eddie, igloo, otter, upstairs) and long vowels (apron, equal, iron, over, unicorn).

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Say a word and identify the vowel sound: like, late, cast, mole, mop, wave, cube, bike, build, mute, male; is it long?

lessons.title: Review
lessons.notes: Closed syllables (shop) and open syllables (she); a vowel that says its name is a long vowel.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: The letter e can be silent; one job of the silent e is to make the other vowel long.

lessons.title: Model
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles and label the vowel and consonants.

objectives.text: explain that a silent e makes the vowel before it say its name
tell short vowels in shop and cap from long vowels in she and cake
say what the silent e does in words like cake and bike
read one-syllable words that end in a vowel, like me, go and hi

replaces: Open Syllables · Y as a vowel (long i)

units.title: a_e
units.summary: Lesson 2: long a with the VCe pattern (cake, name, late). Compare with the short a words from Level 2; sort by word family or short versus long vowel. High-frequency words to map: made, make, take, came, gave, ate.

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear the long a sound in spoken words and segment them into sounds.

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model

lessons.title: Encoding (spelling)
lessons.notes: Sound boxes: match each sound, then add the silent e.

lessons.title: Decoding (reading)
lessons.notes: Spot the VCe pattern, then read the word; short or long vowel?

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and write words from the word list; reading phrases and sentences; dictation.

lessons.title: "Mapping" high-frequency words
lessons.notes: made, make, take, came, gave, ate (the silent e can sit in the last box or outside the boxes)

lessons.title: More practice
lessons.notes: Word sorts by word family or short versus long vowel; student workbook pages.

objectives.text: read words like cake, name, late and game with a long a
spell words with the a_e pattern, such as safe, wave and shake
tell short a words from long a words, like cap and cape
read the common words made, make, take, came, gave and ate

units.title: i_e
units.summary: Lesson 3: long i with the VCe pattern (bike, time, five). High-frequency words to map: like, five, time, ride, white, live (also write).

lessons.title: Phonemic awareness
lessons.notes: Hear the long i sound in spoken words and segment them into sounds.

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles; the first vowel says its name and the e is silent.

lessons.title: Encoding (spelling)
lessons.notes: Sound boxes: match each sound, then add the silent e.

lessons.title: Decoding (reading)
lessons.notes: Spot the VCe pattern, then read the word; short or long vowel?

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and write words from the word list; reading phrases and sentences; dictation.

units.title: u_e
units.summary: Lesson 5: long u with the VCe pattern. Long u has two sounds, /ū/ as in rule and /yū/ as in cube. Regular high-frequency word: use; irregular: sure.

units.title: -se and -ze
units.summary: Lesson 6. The /z/ sound at the end of a silent e word is usually spelled s (nose, use); z is less common. Use can say /yūs/ or /yūz/. Phonemic awareness, mapping and reading words with the final /z/ sound.

units.title: -ce
units.summary: Lesson 7. Job 2 of silent e: when e follows c, the c says /s/ (ice, lace). This is one way to spell the /s/ sound at the end of silent e words, besides s (base, wise). High-frequency words: place, chance, once. Soft c: c says /s/ before e, i or y.

units.title: -ge and -dge
units.summary: Lessons 8a and 8b. Job 3 of silent e: after /j/ at the end of a word, use ge or dge, since j does not end English words. After a short vowel use dge (judge, ridge); after a long vowel or a consonant use ge (page, huge, plunge). ck, tch and dge are used only after short vowels. Words ending in -age and -ure are formed with the same silent e.

lessons.title: Lesson 8a: ge
lessons.notes: Model page and huge; the e makes the vowel long and the g say /j/ (two jobs).

lessons.title: Lesson 8b: dge
lessons.notes: Segment judge, page, ridge, singe, plunge; what comes right before /j/.

units.title: -ve
units.summary: Lesson 9. Job 4 of silent e: English words do not end in v, so a word that ends with /v/ gets a silent e. After a short vowel the silent e does not make the vowel long: delve, give, have, live, solve, twelve, valve. Irregular: dove, love, move. Long vowel words: cave, cove, crave, dive, five, grove, hive, save, stove, wave. High-frequency words: have, give, live.

units.title: Suffix -s and -es with silent e
units.summary: Lesson 10. Adding -s or -es to a silent e word: if the word ends in /j/, /s/ or /z/ the suffix is -es and the e makes its own syllable (noses). Cover the suffix, read the base word first, then count syllables.

units.title: Suffixes -ed and -ing
units.summary: Lesson 11. A vowel suffix (starting with a vowel sound) means dropping the silent e from the base word: hope, hoped, hoping. With one consonant after the vowel the vowel is long; a doubled consonant shows a short vowel (hopping, hopped). Practice words: faked, making, smiled, waving, voted, muting. Dropping y rule: when a word ends in a consonant then y, change y to i before adding suffixes except -ing.

units.title: ar
units.summary: Lesson 1. When a vowel is in front of r it does not make one of its usual sounds; the vowel and r together make a new sound. ar says /ar/ (car, start, hard). High-frequency words: start, part, hard; irregular: are.

lessons.title: Warm-up and review
lessons.notes: Sound deck flip and auditory drill on the graphemes taught so far.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: A vowel in front of r makes a new sound with the r: /ar/ (car).

lessons.title: Modeling decoding
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles; what syllable type is this (r-controlled, "bossy r").

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell words from the word list; sentences and dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: Regular: start, part, hard. Irregular: are

objectives.text: read words like car, farm, start and hard with the ar spelling
say that the vowel and r together make a new sound
spell words such as park, star, dark and scarf using ar
read the common words start, part, hard and are

units.title: or
units.summary: Lesson 2. or says /or/ (for, corn, storm). High-frequency words: for, or (also your and four).

lessons.title: Warm-up and review
lessons.notes: Sound deck flip and auditory drill on the graphemes taught so far.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: A vowel in front of r makes a new sound with the r: /or/ (fork).

lessons.title: Modeling decoding
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles; what syllable type is this (r-controlled, "bossy r").

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell words from the word list; sentences and dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: Regular: for, or

objectives.text: read words like for, fork, corn and storm with the or spelling
tell /or/ in fork from /ar/ in farm
spell words such as horn, sport, north and short using or
read the common words for and or

units.title: er, ir and ur
units.summary: Lesson 3. The /er/ sound is spelled er, ir or ur; there is no sound to tell them apart, so spelling must be learned by word. High-frequency words: first, her, turn, girl; irregular: were.

lessons.title: Warm-up and review
lessons.notes: Sound deck flip and auditory drill on the graphemes taught so far.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: A vowel in front of r makes a new sound with the r: /er/ (her, bird, turn).

lessons.title: Modeling decoding
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles; what syllable type is this (r-controlled, "bossy r").

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell words from the word list; sentences and dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: Regular: first, her, turn, girl. Irregular: were

objectives.text: read words like her, bird, turn, girl and first with the /er/ sound
know that er, ir and ur all say /er/
spell words such as fern, shirt, burn and nurse by learning the right spelling
read the common words first, her, turn and girl

units.title: Review: ar, or, er
units.summary: Lesson 4. Review /ar/, /or/ and /er/ spelled ar, or, er, ir and ur together, with warm-up, word sorts and sentences. Two-syllable words with r-controlled syllables are read and spelled here.

lessons.title: Warm-up
lessons.notes: Sound deck and auditory drill.

lessons.title: Mixed reading
lessons.notes: Words with ar, or, er, ir and ur sorted by sound.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Sentences and spelling.

objectives.text: sort words by whether they have /ar/, /or/ or /er/
read two-syllable words like farmer, corner and thirty
spell dictated words that mix ar, or, er, ir and ur

units.title: ear
units.summary: Lesson 5 (mini-lesson). ear usually says /er/ in the middle of a word (search, earth, heard, earn); the letters can represent three different sounds, as in hear and bear. Only a few one-syllable words use ear for /er/, so students see them all.

lessons.title: Warm-up and review
lessons.notes: Sound deck flip and auditory drill on the graphemes taught so far.

lessons.title: Teaching skill
lessons.notes: A vowel in front of r makes a new sound with the r: /er/ (earth).

lessons.title: Modeling decoding
lessons.notes: Build words with letter tiles; what syllable type is this (r-controlled, "bossy r").

lessons.title: Guided practice
lessons.notes: Read and spell words from the word list; sentences and dictation.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: Show students all the one-syllable /er/ ear words.

objectives.text: read words like search, earth, heard and earn with ear saying /er/
know that ear can say /er/ and use the sound to figure out new words
spell earth, learn and heard by remembering ear
name what type of syllable ear belongs to

units.title: w + ar and w + or
units.summary: Lessons 6.1 and 6.2. When w comes before ar, the ar says /or/ (war, warm, warn, ward, warp). When w comes before or, the or says /er/ (word, work, worm). The same applies after qu. High-frequency words: warm, world, work, word (also watch, wash).

lessons.title: Lesson 6.1: war
lessons.notes: Build warn; w changes the sound, ar says /or/.

lessons.title: Lesson 6.2: wor
lessons.notes: Build word, work and worm; or says /er/ after w.

lessons.title: High-frequency words
lessons.notes: warm, world, work, word.

objectives.text: know that w changes the sound that follows it, as in war and word
read words like war, warm, warn, word, work and worm
spell words such as ward, warp and worth
read the common words warm, world, work and word

units.title: Suffix -er
units.summary: Lessons 7A and 7B. -er has two jobs: more than (brighter, colder, taller, smaller) used to compare two things, and a person who (baker, banker, cheater, boxer); -or can also mean a person who. -est means most. Identify the base word and the suffix in each word.

lessons.title: Lesson 7A: -er, more than
lessons.notes: Review suffixes -s, -es, -ed, -ing; read and spell colder, faster, taller.

lessons.title: Lesson 7B: -er, a person who
lessons.notes: Baker and banker; -er and -or.

lessons.title: Practice
lessons.notes: Break words into base and suffix and use them in sentences.

objectives.text: say that -er can mean more than, as in taller, or a person who, as in baker
read words like brighter, colder, baker and boxer
add -er to a base word and use it in a sentence
name the base word and the suffix in words such as smarter and cheater

units.title: our
units.summary: Lesson 8 (mini-lesson). our says /or/ in some words (four, pour, court, fourth, mourn, source, your). Not many words use it and pronunciation varies (many people say your as yoor), so first grade may simply teach your and four as heart words.

lessons.notes: your, four (heart words in first grade)

objectives.text: read words like four, pour, court and fourth with our saying /or/

units.title: /ū/: oo
units.summary: Lesson 1. oo spells /ū/ (moon, food, zoom, pool). The sound /ū/ can also be spelled ew, ue and ui. Connect the word too to its meaning. High-frequency words: too, soon.

lessons.notes: oo says /ū/ as in moon, food and zoom. There are two long u sounds, /ū/ and /yū/.

lessons.notes: Word lists, sentences, dictation.

lessons.notes: too, soon

objectives.text: read words like moon, food, zoom and pool with oo saying /ū/

lessons.title: Teaching skill and model

spell words such as grew, true, clue and chew using ew or ue
read the common words new, few and blue

units.title: /ū/ in the middle: ui
